sections.text:
تستخدم هذه الطريقة لمعرفة وجود المياه والرواسب فى زيوت التزييت وزيوت العزل 
 الكهربية (ان كان هناك شك فى وجودها بزيوت العزل) ولتحديد تلوثلها بالماء 
 والمواد الصلبة الغريبة (اتربة شوائب اخرى مثل الصدأ او جزيئات دقيقة ناتجة من 
 برى المعادن).

قام بإعداد هذا المستند الكيميائي/ 
 اشرف صلاح الدين صالح وتم مراجعة المستند 
 بمعرفة الكيميائي/ 
 خالد بسطاوى مكى محسب وقام بالاختبار السيدة الكيميائية/ 
 مرفت صالح سيد احمد وتم اعتماده من الكيميائى/ 
 محمد وجدى عبد الله 
 مدير عام بمحطة كهرباء السد العالى بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء وموثق من المهندس/ 
 عبد النبى عبد الغنى عبد النبى 
 رئيس قطاع المحطة بشركة 
 المحطات المائية 
 لإنتاج الكهرباء.

وهذا المستند معتمد من المهندس/ 
 محمد اسامة سليمان سليم منسق الـMPIS بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء.

rows: معرفة تلوث الزيت بالمياه والرواسب والتى تؤثر سلبا على كفاءته.

يتم اخذ العينة بالطريقة السليمة السالف ذكرها طبقا للـ 
 (MPIS(Oil-013-r2.

تأكد من صحة البيانات الواردة 
 على العينة.
تأكد من عدم تعرض العينة لضوء الشمس المباشر.

اترك العينة فترة تكفى لترسيب المياه والرواسب اسفل 
 زجاجة العينة ( 3 ساعات لزيوت التزييت ، 1 ساعة لزيوت العزل).
تجنب انسكاب الزيت على الارض واذا حدث ذلك يتم ازالته.

يراعى تشغيل الشفاط للتخلص من الابخرة المتصاعدة اثناء اجراء الاختبار وترك 
 النوافذ مفتوحة.

مصدر لهب - ماصة جافة (10مم) - انبوبة اختبار جافة - ماسك - مضخة مطاطية - 
 بونقة نظيفة بيضاء.
اشعل مصدر اللهب واجعله بعيدا عن تيارات الهواء.
جفف كل من انبوبة الاختبار والماصة على اللهب باستخدام الماصة.

اسحب كمية من 
 الزيت بالماصة ويراعى مسح قاع العينة بالماصة لسحب جميع المياه والرواسب.

قم بتفريغ الماصة 
 فى انبوبة الاختبار وان تعذر ذلك (فى حالة زيوت التزييت) استخدم المدخة.

جفف انبوبة الاختبار من الخارج من اى اثار زيت قبل 
 وضعها على اللهب.

عن طريق الماسك ضع انبوبة الاختبار على اللهب ويتم 
 التسخين.

يجب الالتزام بالهدوء التام حتى سماع الفرقعة (وهذا 
 القياس يوضح اقل نسبة من الماء مهما كانت ضئيلة).

قياس الرواسب : تختبر 
 بمجرد النظر حيث يجب ان يكون زيت المحولات خالى تماما من اى رواسب اما 
 بالنسبة لزيوت التزييت علاوة على النظر توضع نواتج اختبار الفرقعة فى بوتقة 
 بيضاء ويتم من خلالها التأكد من وجود الرواسب.

ملحوطة : اختبار المياه والرواسب متلازمان 
 وتسخدم هذه الطريقة لجميع معدات المحطات التابعة للشركة حيث لم تنص تعليمات 
 المصنع والمواصفات على تحديد نسبة اى منهما ولكن معرفة وجودها من عدمة.

Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: Oil-018-r0a
Equipment: Test method for water & sediment by cracking & visually
Issued to: High Dam Power Station
Document Status: Approved
Document Approval Date: 19 January 2009
Procedure: According to russian method
Date of Next Review: January 2014

sections_en.text: This method is used to detect the presence of water and sediment in lubricating oils and electrical insulating oils (if their presence in insulating oils is suspected), and to determine their contamination with water and foreign solid materials (dust, other impurities such as rust, or fine particles resulting from metal wear).

This document was prepared by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, reviewed by the chemist Khaled Bastawy Makki Mohasseb, tested by the chemist Mervat Saleh Sayed Ahmed, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.

rows: Detecting oil contamination with water and sediment, which adversely affect its efficiency.
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2).
Make sure the data on the sample are correct.
Make sure the sample is not exposed to direct sunlight.
Leave the sample for a period sufficient for the water and sediment to settle at the bottom of the sample bottle (3 hours for lubricating oils, 1 hour for insulating oils).
Avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it.
Operate the fume hood to remove the vapours rising during the test, and leave the windows open.
Flame source - dry pipette (10 mm) - dry test tube - holder - rubber pump - clean white crucible.
Light the flame source and keep it away from air currents.
Dry both the test tube and the pipette over the flame using the pipette.
Draw a quantity of oil with the pipette, taking care to sweep the bottom of the sample with the pipette to draw off all the water and sediment.
Empty the pipette into the test tube; if this is not possible (in the case of lubricating oils), use the pump.
Dry the test tube from the outside of any traces of oil before placing it on the flame.
Using the holder, place the test tube on the flame and heat it.
Complete silence must be observed until the crackling is heard (this measurement shows the smallest proportion of water, however slight).

Sediment measurement: tested by visual inspection only, as transformer oil must be completely free of any sediment. For lubricating oils, in addition to visual inspection, the products of the crackle test are placed in a white crucible to confirm the presence of sediment.

Note: the water and sediment tests go together, and this method is used for all station equipment belonging to the Company, as the manufacturer instructions and specifications do not specify a percentage for either of them; only their presence or absence is determined.

Document No.: Oil-018-r0a | Equipment: Test method for water & sediment by cracking & visually
Issued to: High Dam Power Station
Document Status: Approved
Document Approval Date: 19 January 2009 | Procedure: According to russian method
Date of Next Review: January 2014
Introduction
This method is used to detect the presence of water and sediment in lubricating oils and electrical insulating oils (if their presence in insulating oils is suspected), and to determine their contamination with water and foreign solid materials (dust, other impurities such as rust, or fine particles resulting from metal wear).
This document was prepared by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, reviewed by the chemist Khaled Bastawy Makki Mohasseb, tested by the chemist Mervat Saleh Sayed Ahmed, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
Objective
Detecting oil contamination with water and sediment, which adversely affect its efficiency. | 
Procedures Required for Measurement Accuracy
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2). | 
Make sure the data on the sample are correct. | 
Make sure the sample is not exposed to direct sunlight. | 
Leave the sample for a period sufficient for the water and sediment to settle at the bottom of the sample bottle (3 hours for lubricating oils, 1 hour for insulating oils). | 
Environmental Recommendations
Avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it. | 1.
Operate the fume hood to remove the vapours rising during the test, and leave the windows open. | 2.
Tools and Materials Used
Flame source - dry pipette (10 mm) - dry test tube - holder - rubber pump - clean white crucible. | 1.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Test Steps
Light the flame source and keep it away from air currents. | 1.
Dry both the test tube and the pipette over the flame using the pipette. | 2.
Draw a quantity of oil with the pipette, taking care to sweep the bottom of the sample with the pipette to draw off all the water and sediment. | 3.
Empty the pipette into the test tube; if this is not possible (in the case of lubricating oils), use the pump. | 4.
Dry the test tube from the outside of any traces of oil before placing it on the flame. | 5.
Using the holder, place the test tube on the flame and heat it. | 6.
Complete silence must be observed until the crackling is heard (this measurement shows the smallest proportion of water, however slight). | 7.
Sediment measurement: tested by visual inspection only, as transformer oil must be completely free of any sediment. For lubricating oils, in addition to visual inspection, the products of the crackle test are placed in a white crucible to confirm the presence of sediment.
Note: the water and sediment tests go together, and this method is used for all station equipment belonging to the Company, as the manufacturer instructions and specifications do not specify a percentage for either of them; only their presence or absence is determined.
